q: What is the youngest age at which a Michigan teen can get a Level 1 Learner's License?
exp: Level 1 is available at 14 years 9 months, after Segment 1. Segment 1 itself can start a month earlier, at 14 years 8 months.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Under 18, GDL; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: Before a Michigan teen takes the driving skills test, how many hours of supervised driving must be logged?
exp: The log must show at least 50 hours, with at least 10 at night. The 30 and 2 figure is the earlier requirement for starting Segment 2.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driving skills test; MCL 257.310e (legislature.mi.gov)

q: During which hours may a Level 2 driver NOT drive unless an exception applies?
exp: Level 2 drivers may not drive from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. unless supervised, driving for work or going to or from an authorized activity.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 2; MCL 257.310e(6) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Under Level 2 rules, how many passengers under 21 may ride with a teen driver when no exception applies?
exp: A Level 2 driver may carry no more than one passenger under 21, unless a supervising adult rides along, the riders are family, or the trip is for work or an authorized activity.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 2; MCL 257.310e(6) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Under Kelsey's Law, when may a Level 1 or Level 2 driver use a cell phone while driving?
a: Whenever the phone is in hands-free mode
b: Only to report an emergency such as a crash or crime
c: Only while stopped at a red light
d: Only for calls to a parent or guardian
exp: Kelsey's Law bars Level 1 and Level 2 drivers from phone use while driving, even hands-free, except to report an emergency.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1; Ch. 4, Cell phone use; SOS FAQ, Drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/drivers-under-18)

q: What score must a teen earn to pass the Segment 1 state exam in driver education?
exp: Both the Segment 1 and Segment 2 state exams require at least 70 percent.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driver education Segment 1; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: How long must a teen hold a Level 1 Learner's License before moving up to Level 2?
exp: Level 2 requires age 16 and at least 6 months on Level 1. Three months is the wait before Segment 2.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 2; MCL 257.310e(5) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: To qualify for Level 2, a teen must have no violations or at-fault crashes during how many days before applying?
exp: The record must be free of convictions, civil infractions, suspensions and at-fault crashes for the 90 days before the Level 2 application.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 2; MCL 257.310e(5) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: An adult with a new temporary instruction permit (TIP) must practice for at least how long before the driving skills test?
exp: Adults must practice at least 30 days with a licensed adult on a TIP before taking the skills test.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Temporary instruction permit; SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: How is the SOS knowledge test for adults set up?
a: It has an Operator part and a Signs part, and you must pass both
b: It is one combined test scored as a whole
c: It is a Signs test only, since laws are tested on the road
d: It has two parts, and a high Operator score can cover a weak Signs score
exp: The test has an Operator section on laws and safe driving and a separate Signs section; both must be passed.
src: SOS online testing page (michigan.gov/SOSOnlineTesting); SOS news release, online testing for adults

q: At what age may a Michigan teen start Segment 1 of driver education?
exp: Segment 1 may start at 14 years 8 months with a parent or guardian's permission.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driver education Segment 1; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: How many hours of classroom instruction does Segment 1 require at a minimum?
exp: Segment 1 includes at least 24 classroom hours, at no more than 2 hours a day.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driver education Segment 1; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: How much behind-the-wheel instruction does Segment 1 include at a minimum?
exp: Segment 1 includes at least 6 hours driving with an instructor, plus 4 hours of observation.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driver education Segment 1; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: Before starting Segment 2, a teen must have held Level 1 for 3 months and logged how many supervised hours?
exp: Segment 2 requires 3 months on Level 1 and a log of at least 30 hours with at least 2 at night.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driver education Segment 2; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: Who may supervise a Level 1 driver?
b: Any licensed adult 21 or older, with or without a parent's permission
d: A licensed parent or guardian, or a licensed adult 21 or older designated by them
exp: The supervisor must be a licensed parent or guardian, or a licensed adult 21 or older with a signed letter from the parent or guardian.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 1; MCL 257.310e(4) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the earliest age for a Level 3 Full License?
exp: Level 3 comes at 17 after at least 6 months on Level 2 and 12 months in a row without violations.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 3; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: To advance to Level 3, how long must a teen go without a moving violation, at-fault crash, suspension or GDL violation?
exp: Level 3 requires 12 consecutive months with a clean record.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, GDL Level 3; MCL 257.310e(9) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the SOS fee for a Level 1 Learner's License?
exp: The Level 1 Learner's License costs $25.
src: SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: How long is a Michigan temporary instruction permit (TIP) valid?
exp: A TIP is valid for 180 days; if you do not pass the skills test in that time, you need a new TIP.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Temporary instruction permit; SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: What does the online version of the SOS knowledge test cost?
exp: The online test carries a $6.50 convenience fee for each attempt; the test at an SOS office is free.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, 18 and older; SOS online testing page (michigan.gov/SOSOnlineTesting); SOS news release, online testing for adults

q: Who may take the SOS knowledge test online at home?
d: Only new residents from another state
exp: The online test is offered to residents 18 and older whose driving privileges are not suspended, revoked or denied.
src: SOS online testing page (michigan.gov/SOSOnlineTesting); SOS news release, online testing for adults

q: Once you pass the SOS knowledge test, how long does the result stay valid?
exp: A passed knowledge test is valid for one year.
src: SOS online testing page (michigan.gov/SOSOnlineTesting); SOS news release, online testing for adults

q: If you take the knowledge test at an SOS office, how early should you arrive before closing?
exp: Arrive at least one hour before closing so there is time to finish the test.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Vision and knowledge tests

q: How many proofs of Michigan residency must you bring when applying?
d: None if you bring a passport
exp: At least two residency documents are required, such as a recent utility bill and a bank statement.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Providing proof of residency

q: How long is every new Michigan driver on probation, at a minimum?
exp: All new drivers, teens and adults, are on probation for at least three years.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Probationary license program; SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: To finish probation on time, which part of it must be free of traffic convictions, suspensions and at-fault crashes?
exp: The final 10 months of probation must be clean, or probation is extended.
src: SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older); SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: What happens when a Level 2 driver breaks a Level 2 restriction?
a: The license is canceled and Segment 1 must be repeated
b: Only a warning letter goes to the parent
c: It is a misdemeanor with 6 points
d: It is a civil infraction with 2 points, and Level 2 is extended 12 months
exp: A Level 2 violation is a civil infraction that adds 2 points; the parent is notified and Level 2 lasts 12 more months.
src: SOS FAQ, Drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/faqs/license-and-id/drivers-under-18); MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the minimum age to take the driving skills test as a teen?
exp: A teen must be at least 15, with 6 months on Level 1, Segment 2 done and 50 logged hours.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driving skills test; SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18)

q: What are the three parts of the Michigan driving skills test, in order?
a: Vision test, basic control skills, on-road test
b: Vehicle inspection, basic control skills, on-road test
c: On-road test, parallel parking, vehicle inspection
d: Vehicle inspection, written signs test, on-road test
exp: The test starts with a vehicle inspection, then basic control skills on a closed course, then the on-road test.
src: SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18); SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)

q: In the basic control skills part of the road test, how many errors may you make and still pass?
exp: You pass the basic control skills part with six errors or fewer.
src: SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)

q: On the on-road part of the Michigan driving skills test, what is the most points you can lose and still pass?
exp: You pass the on-road test with 25 points or fewer; more than 25 is a fail.
src: SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)

q: How often may you take the driving skills test?
exp: Only one driving skills test may be taken in a 24-hour period.
src: SOS, New drivers under 18 (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-under-18); SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: A new resident holds a valid license from another state. What must they pass for a Michigan license?
a: The knowledge test and a vision test
c: The knowledge test, a TIP and the skills test
d: A road sign test and a vision test
exp: Drivers from another U.S. state convert with a vision test; no written test, TIP or skills test is needed.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Michigan and REAL ID / Moved to Michigan

q: Holders of a valid license from which country can switch to a Michigan license without the written test, TIP or skills test?
exp: Michigan lets drivers licensed in Canada, Germany or South Korea convert without those tests.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Moved to Michigan; Driving skills test

q: Your out-of-state license expired five years ago. What do you need for a Michigan license?
b: Only a renewal fee and a photo
d: A TIP and a driving skills test
exp: A license expired for at least four years means applying for a TIP and passing the driving skills test.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Moved to Michigan

q: A person who has never been licensed applies for a license with two moving violation convictions in the past three years. What happens?
a: The license is issued on probation
b: The license is issued after a vision test
d: A license is issued with a 10 p.m. curfew
exp: Michigan will not issue a license to a never-licensed applicant with two or more moving violation convictions within three years.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Licensing requirements

q: What does the SOS charge for an enhanced driver's license?
exp: A standard license costs $25 and an enhanced license $45. The enhanced card is REAL ID compliant.
src: SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: A Michigan school zone limit may be lowered below the normal limit, but never below what speed?
exp: A school zone limit can be up to 20 mph below the normal limit, but never under 25 mph.
src: MCL 257.627a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Unless signs show a different limit, what is the speed limit in a Michigan work zone posted for reduced speed?
exp: Most posted Michigan work zones carry a 45 mph limit, sometimes only while workers are present.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Speed limits; Construction zones

q: What happens to fines for moving violations in a Michigan work zone?
c: They stay the same, but points double
exp: Fines double for all moving violations in a work zone, and speeding there adds extra points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Construction zones

q: How many points does speeding more than 15 mph over the limit in a Michigan work zone add?
exp: Work zone speeding adds 3 points at 10 mph or less over, 4 at 11 to 15 mph over, and 5 above that.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Construction zones; MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Near a Michigan school, when does the lower school zone limit usually start?
c: Up to 30 minutes before school begins, as the sign shows
exp: The school limit applies during the posted times, which start no more than 30 minutes before the first session.
src: MCL 257.627a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: In Michigan, a five-sided sign shaped like a house warns of what?
b: A school zone or school crossing
exp: The pentagon is used only for school zones and school crossings.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs

q: On a Michigan road, what does a fluorescent pink sign mean?
a: An incident, emergency or other unplanned event ahead
exp: Fluorescent pink marks incident management, such as a crash scene.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs, Traffic sign colors

q: What does a brown sign tell you?
a: Where services such as gas are
c: That trucks must use another route
d: Where to find a recreation or cultural area
exp: Brown signs point to recreation and cultural places, such as parks.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs, Traffic sign colors

q: What does an orange warning sign tell you?
c: Construction or maintenance work is ahead
d: The road is a scenic route
exp: Orange signs warn of construction or maintenance areas.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs, Traffic sign colors

q: Blue signs along a Michigan highway show what?
b: Services such as gas, food and lodging
exp: Blue is used for motorist services and hospitality.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs, Traffic sign colors

q: What does a fluorescent yellow-green sign warn you about?
exp: Fluorescent yellow-green signals caution for schools, pedestrians and bicyclists.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signs, Traffic sign colors

q: An orange triangle on the back of a farm vehicle or buggy means the vehicle travels no faster than what speed?
exp: The slow-moving vehicle emblem marks vehicles that do not go faster than 25 mph.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 30

q: Where is this yellow pennant-shaped sign placed, and what does it mean?
a: On the right side of the road; passing lane ahead
b: Over the center lane; left turns only
c: On the left side of the road; do not pass
d: On the left side of the road; road narrows
exp: The pennant stands on the left side and marks the start of a no passing zone.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 40

q: What does a Pass With Care sign mark?
a: The start of a passing lane for trucks
b: The end of a no passing zone
c: A zone where passing is never allowed
d: A curve where you must pass on the right
exp: Pass With Care follows a Do Not Pass sign and marks where passing may resume when safe.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 21

q: You see this sign ahead of you. What has happened?
a: You are driving against traffic and must get out safely
b: A one-way street begins to your right
c: The road ends and you must turn
d: You are entering a freeway ramp correctly
exp: Wrong Way means you have entered a lane of oncoming traffic.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 25

q: A freeway median crossover is marked Authorized Vehicles Only. Who may use it?
a: Any driver who missed an exit
b: Only police, emergency and maintenance vehicles
c: Any driver once traffic is clear
exp: Never use a median crossover; drive to the next exit instead.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 24

q: What does this sign mean?
d: A railroad crossing; yield to trains
exp: The crossbuck marks a railroad crossing; look and be ready to stop for trains.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 27

q: What must you do at this sign?
a: Slow down and go if the road looks clear
b: Stop only if other cars are present
c: Come to a complete stop and yield before going on
exp: The octagon means a full stop, then yield to traffic and pedestrians.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 13

q: What does this sign tell you to do?
b: Slow down and let crossing traffic go first
exp: Yield means slow down, be ready to stop and let vehicles crossing your path go.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 14

q: What does this warning sign mean?
a: Two-way traffic begins ahead; keep right
exp: This sign warns that traffic will soon travel in both directions on your road.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 50

q: What does this sign warn you about?
d: The divided highway ends and traffic will be two-way
exp: Divided Highway Ends means the median is ending.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 49

q: What does this sign tell you?
c: Your lane is ending; prepare to merge
exp: A lane ends sign means you must merge and yield to traffic in the other lane.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 48

q: What does this sign warn you about?
b: The road is slippery when wet
exp: Slippery When Wet warns that the surface can get slick in rain or bad weather.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 52

q: What does this sign mean?
a: The center lane is only for left turns
c: Use the center lane to pass
exp: Center Lane Left Turn Only reserves the middle lane for left turns from either direction.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 19

q: What does this warning sign mean?
d: A side road enters ahead; watch for traffic
exp: Side Road Ahead warns that a road joins from the side shown.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 42

q: What does this sign warn you about?
c: Traffic may merge into your road from the side
exp: The merge sign warns of traffic joining from the side; adjust your speed to let it in.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 47

q: What does this sign tell you?
b: Crews are working ahead; drive with care
exp: The orange Road Work Ahead sign means construction or maintenance crews are in the area.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 44

q: What does this sign mean?
a: Traffic flows only in the direction of the arrow
b: Turn only in the direction of the arrow
exp: One Way means all lanes carry traffic in the same direction.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 5

q: What does this sign mean?
b: The road curves back on itself
exp: No U Turn prohibits turning around at that place.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 17

q: A Bridge Ices Before Road sign is warning you that:
a: The bridge is closed in winter
b: Trucks may not cross in snow
c: The bridge can be icy even when the road is clear
d: Salt is not used on the bridge
exp: Bridges freeze before the road, so slow down even if the road looks dry.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic sign challenge answers, No. 4

q: In Michigan, onto which street may you turn left on a steady red light after a full stop?
b: A one-way street, but only from another one-way street
c: No street; left on red is never allowed
d: A one-way street whose traffic flows in the direction of your turn
exp: Michigan allows left on red onto a one-way street from either a one-way or a two-way street, after a full stop and yielding.
src: MCL 257.612(1)(c) (legislature.mi.gov); What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Right of way when turning

q: At a left turn signal, you face a steady red arrow pointing left. The cross street is a two-way street. What may you do?
a: Turn left after a full stop
b: Turn left without stopping if the way is clear
c: Wait; do not turn until the signal changes
d: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic
exp: A red arrow follows the red light rules for its turn, and Michigan allows a left on red only onto a one-way street. Onto a two-way street, wait for the signal to change.
src: MCL 257.612(1) and (1)(c)(ii) (legislature.mi.gov); What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Flashing yellow arrow left-turn signal head

q: Turning left on red from a two-way street onto a one-way street in Michigan, whom must you also yield to?
exp: After a full stop, check traffic from the right and yield to vehicles opposite you that are turning right.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Figure 4.3

q: In Michigan, what must you do before turning right on a steady red light?
a: Stop completely and yield to pedestrians and cross traffic
b: Slow down and turn if no cars are coming
c: Wait for the light to turn green
exp: A right on red is legal after a full stop and yielding, unless a sign prohibits it.
src: MCL 257.612(1)(c) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: In Michigan, where is the red light on a vertical traffic signal?
exp: The red light is on top of a Michigan traffic signal.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Traffic signals

q: What may you do when a flashing yellow arrow is lit for your left turn?
a: Turn left; oncoming traffic is stopped
b: Stop and wait for a green arrow
c: Turn left after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians
d: Turn only if a sign allows it
exp: A flashing yellow arrow permits a left turn once oncoming traffic, which has a green light, leaves a safe gap.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Flashing yellow arrow

q: When a Michigan school bus has its red overhead lights flashing, how far from the bus must you stop?
exp: Michigan drivers must stop at least 20 feet from a school bus with flashing red lights.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, School buses

q: On a Michigan road, when must you slow down by at least 10 mph below the posted limit?
a: When passing any car on the shoulder
d: When passing a stopped emergency vehicle with its lights flashing
exp: The Move Over law requires slowing at least 10 mph below the limit and moving over a lane when you can.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Emergency vehicles; MCL 257.653a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How far must you stay behind a moving emergency vehicle that has its lights and siren on in Michigan?
exp: Stay at least 500 feet behind any moving emergency vehicle using lights and a siren.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Emergency vehicles

q: A school bus with red lights flashing is stopped on the other side of a highway divided by a grass median. What must you do?
b: Continue with care; you need not stop
exp: Traffic on the other side of a highway divided by a barrier such as a median does not have to stop.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, School buses, Figure 4.1

q: What do flashing yellow overhead lights on a Michigan school bus mean?
a: Prepare to stop; the bus is about to stop
c: The bus is out of service
d: The bus is letting children off now
exp: Flashing yellow overhead lights warn that the red lights will soon come on.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, School bus signals

q: What happens to the fine for failing to stop for a Michigan school bus?
a: It is the same as any moving violation
b: It is triple the usual fine
c: A warning is issued the first time
d: It is double the usual fine
exp: School bus fines are double, and the violation adds 3 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, School buses; Ch. 2, Point system

q: When an emergency vehicle with lights and siren approaches, what does the Michigan manual say to do with your foot after you stop?
a: Rest it on the gas so you can move quickly
c: Keep it on the brake so your brake lights show
exp: Holding the brake lets the emergency driver see that you have stopped.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Emergency vehicles

q: Which vehicle may you pass while it is responding with flashing lights and a siren?
a: A fire truck going under 30 mph
b: None, unless its driver or an officer waves you on
d: A police car in the right lane
exp: Never pass a moving emergency vehicle using its lights and siren unless directed to.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Emergency vehicles

q: Funeral processions in Michigan must yield to which vehicles?
a: Fire trucks, ambulances and police vehicles
exp: Funeral processions have the right of way over all vehicles except fire, ambulance and police.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Right of way and funerals

q: Which stopped vehicles are covered as emergency vehicles by Michigan's Move Over rule?
c: Any car with hazard lights on
d: Police, fire and ambulance vehicles, plus marked tow trucks and road service vehicles
exp: The definition includes clearly marked tow trucks and road service vehicles with flashing lights.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Emergency vehicles

q: How do you turn left at an intersection that uses a Michigan Left?
a: Drive through or turn right, then make a U-turn at the median crossover
b: Turn left from the center lane at the light
c: Turn left on a green arrow only
d: Make a left from the right lane
exp: At a Michigan Left, direct left turns are banned; you use a marked median crossover to U-turn instead.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Michigan Lefts

q: A median crossover at a Michigan Left has no markings showing two lanes. How should you treat it?
a: As two lanes, side by side
d: As a single lane, one vehicle turning at a time
exp: An unmarked crossover is always a single-lane crossover; the extra width is for large vehicles.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 5, Michigan Lefts

q: Does Michigan law set a distance in feet for signaling before a turn?
c: No; you must signal, but no distance is set
exp: The Michigan Vehicle Code requires a signal before turning or stopping but does not set a distance in feet.
src: MCL 257.648 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: If you miss your exit on a Michigan freeway, what should you do?
b: Drive to the next exit and come back
d: Stop and wait for a gap to back up
exp: Never back up or use a crossover; take the next exit.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Leaving a freeway

q: When there are two right-turn lanes, which lane should you end in after turning?
a: The lane that matches the lane you turned from
exp: With multiple turn lanes, finish your turn in the corresponding lane.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Right turns

q: What is the speed limit on Michigan freeways unless signs show otherwise?
exp: Michigan freeways allow 70 mph and require at least 55 mph unless posted otherwise.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Speed limits

q: What following distance does the Michigan manual require?
d: At least 6 seconds at all times
exp: Keep a 3 to 4 second gap, and increase it to 6 seconds or more at high speed or in bad conditions.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Stopping distances

q: How many points does speeding 11 to 15 mph over the limit add to a Michigan record?
exp: Points for speeding: 1 to 5 over is 1, 6 to 10 is 2, 11 to 15 is 3, and more than 15 is 4.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system; MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the speed limit in a Michigan platted subdivision unless posted otherwise?
exp: Subdivisions and condominium complexes default to 25 mph.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Speed limits

q: What is the Michigan speed limit on a highway that is not a freeway, unless posted otherwise?
exp: Unless posted, non-freeway highways and streets default to 55 mph.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Speed limits

q: How many points does speeding more than 15 mph over the limit add in Michigan, outside a work zone?
exp: Speeding more than 15 mph over adds 4 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system; MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How many points does speeding 1 to 5 mph over the limit add in Michigan?
exp: Speeding 1 to 5 mph over adds 1 point.
src: MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How far ahead does the Michigan manual tell you to look while driving?
exp: Scanning 20 to 30 seconds ahead helps you spot hazards early.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Stopping distances

q: When rain first begins, how much following distance should you allow?
c: At least twice the normal distance
exp: Roads are slickest in the first half hour of rain; at least double your following distance.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Rain and fog

q: A Michigan HOV lane is in effect during rush hour. How many people must be in your vehicle to use it?
c: Only the driver if the car is electric
exp: HOV lanes during posted hours require two or more occupants; motorcycles may use them at any time.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Freeway driving

q: On a Michigan two-lane road, how close may you get to an oncoming vehicle before you must be back in your lane after passing?
exp: You must return to your lane before coming within 200 feet of any oncoming vehicle.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Passing on the left

q: Within how many feet of an intersection or railroad crossing is passing banned in Michigan?
exp: Do not pass within 100 feet of an intersection or railroad crossing.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, When passing is prohibited

q: On a Michigan freeway with three or more lanes in your direction, which lane may you use?
a: Any lane, but stay right if you drive near the minimum speed
d: Only the left lane when passing
exp: With three or more lanes, any lane may be used; slow drivers keep right.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Freeway driving

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in Michigan?
exp: Michigan bans parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: In Michigan, you may not park within how many feet of a stop sign, traffic light or flashing beacon?
exp: Parking within 30 feet of a stop sign, signal or flashing beacon is not allowed.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: When parallel parked in Michigan, your car may be no more than how far from the curb?
exp: A parked car must be within 12 inches of the curb.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: How close to the nearest rail of a railroad crossing may you park in Michigan?
exp: Parking within 50 feet of the nearest rail is banned.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: In Michigan, you may not park within how many feet of a marked crosswalk?
exp: Michigan bans parking within 20 feet of a marked crosswalk, or 15 feet of an intersection with no crosswalk.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: How far from a fire or a crash must you stay when parking in Michigan?
exp: Never park within 500 feet of a fire or a crash.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Parking violations

q: What is the minimum distance Michigan law requires when you pass a bicycle?
exp: Michigan requires at least 3 feet when passing a bicyclist; some cities require 5 feet.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Bicyclists; MCL 257.636 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: May you pass a bicyclist in a Michigan no passing zone?
a: Yes, if it is safe to do so
c: Only if the rider waves you on
d: Only on roads posted 25 mph or less
exp: Michigan law allows passing a bicycle in a no passing zone when it is safe.
src: MCL 257.636(3) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What following distance does the Michigan manual give behind a motorcycle, moped or bicycle?
exp: Tailgating is illegal; leave at least 3 or 4 seconds behind these riders.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Sharing the road

q: Is a Michigan bicyclist required to ride in a bike lane when one is present?
d: No; riders may leave it to turn left or avoid hazards
exp: Bicyclists are not required to use a bike lane.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 6, Bicyclists

q: When must Michigan drivers have their headlights on?
b: From one hour after sunset to one hour before sunrise
c: From one half hour after sunset to one half hour before sunrise
exp: Headlights are required from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, and whenever visibility is poor.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Driving at night

q: In Michigan, you may not use or flash your high beams within how many feet of an oncoming vehicle?
exp: High beams must be off within 500 feet of oncoming traffic.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Driving at night; MCL 257.700 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: After a Michigan crash, when must you notify the police?
a: When anyone is injured or damage is more than $1,000
d: Only if the other driver asks
exp: Call police if there are injuries or more than $1,000 in property damage.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Crashes

q: Headlights are required whenever you cannot clearly see people and vehicles at what distance?
exp: Turn on headlights whenever there is not enough light to see clearly at 500 feet.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Driving at night

q: A deer runs in front of your car and a crash cannot be avoided. What does the Michigan manual say to do?
c: Brake firmly and stay in your lane
d: Flash your high beams and honk
exp: Do not veer for deer; swerving often causes worse crashes.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Vehicle deer crashes

q: After a minor Michigan crash with no serious injuries, what should you do with a car that can still be driven?
a: Leave it where it stopped for police
b: Move it off the main road to a safe spot
c: Drive home and report it later
exp: Michigan law calls for moving drivable vehicles off the main roadway when no one is seriously hurt.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Crashes

q: During a Michigan traffic stop, what does the State Police advise you to do with your hands?
a: Keep both hands on the steering wheel
b: Hold your license out the window
d: Reach for your papers right away
exp: Stay in the car, lower the window and keep both hands visible on the wheel.
src: Michigan State Police, What to expect during a traffic stop (michigan.gov/msp)

q: Which documents should you show a Michigan officer at a traffic stop when asked?
d: License, registration and proof of insurance
exp: Officers ask for your driver's license, vehicle registration and proof of insurance.
src: Michigan State Police, What to expect during a traffic stop (michigan.gov/msp)

q: In fog during the day, which lights should you use in Michigan?
exp: Use low beams in fog, rain or snow; high beams reflect back.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 7, Driving at night; Rain and fog

q: What is the BAC level at which a Michigan driver under 21 breaks the law?
exp: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.02 or more, or with any alcohol in the body from drinking.
src: MCL 257.625(6) (legislature.mi.gov); Michigan State Police, Impaired driving law

q: What is the license suspension for a first refusal of a chemical test in Michigan?
exp: A first refusal brings a 1-year suspension; a second within 7 years, 2 years.
src: MCL 257.625f (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Under Michigan's hands-free law, what is the fine for a first offense of holding a phone while driving?
exp: The fine is $100 for a first offense and $250 for later ones; fines double if you cause a crash.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Distracted driving; MCL 257.602b (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Michigan's high BAC law covers drivers with a BAC of at least what level?
exp: A BAC of 0.17 or more brings tougher penalties.
src: MCL 257.625(1)(c) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the maximum jail time for a first Michigan OWI conviction with a BAC under 0.17?
exp: A first OWI carries up to 93 days in jail and a $100 to $500 fine.
src: MCL 257.625(9) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the fine range for a first OWI with a BAC of 0.17 or more in Michigan?
exp: A first high BAC conviction carries a $200 to $700 fine and up to 180 days in jail.
src: MCL 257.625(9) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How long is the license suspended after a first Michigan OWI conviction with a BAC under 0.17?
b: 180 days, with no driving for the first 30
exp: The suspension lasts 180 days; a restricted license is not available during the first 30.
src: MCL 257.319(8) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: After a first high BAC conviction, how can a Michigan driver get restricted driving privileges?
a: After 45 days, with an ignition interlock in the vehicle
exp: High BAC means a 1-year suspension; restricted driving is possible after 45 days only with an ignition interlock.
src: MCL 257.319(8) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How many points does a Michigan OWI conviction add to your record?
exp: Operating while intoxicated adds 6 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: A Michigan driver under 21 is convicted of driving with a BAC of 0.03. What is the maximum fine for a first offense?
exp: Under 21 at 0.02 up to 0.08: up to $250, up to 360 hours of community service and 4 points.
src: MCL 257.625(12) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How many points does a Michigan driver under 21 get for driving with any bodily alcohol content?
exp: The manual lists 4 points for drivers under 21 with any bodily alcohol content.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: What happens to the license of a Michigan driver under 21 after a first conviction for driving with a BAC of 0.02 up to 0.08?
a: A 30-day suspension, which may be a restricted license
exp: The license is suspended for 30 days, and the SOS may allow restricted driving for all or part of it.
src: MCL 257.319(8)(c) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Under 21, what happens if you refuse a roadside preliminary breath test in Michigan?
d: 2 points are added to your record
exp: Refusing a preliminary breath test under 21 adds 2 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: What is the maximum fine for a first offense of buying, drinking or possessing alcohol under 21 in Michigan?
exp: A first minor in possession violation is a civil infraction with a fine of up to $100.
src: MCL 436.1703 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Using a fake ID to buy alcohol in Michigan can bring up to how much jail time?
exp: Using fraudulent ID to buy alcohol is a misdemeanor punishable by up to 93 days in jail.
src: MCL 436.1703(2) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: A Michigan driver is convicted of a drug possession offense while not driving. What happens to the license for a first offense?
b: Nothing, since no car was involved
exp: Drug convictions suspend the license even if you were not driving: 6 months with no prior drug violations.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Alcohol and drugs

q: Where may an opened bottle of alcohol be carried in a Michigan vehicle?
c: On the back seat if a passenger is 21
d: In the trunk or another area outside the passenger area
exp: Open alcohol may not be in the passenger area; keep it in the trunk or a space separate from passengers.
src: MCL 257.624a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Which phone use is allowed for a Michigan driver with a regular license?
a: Reading a text at a red light
b: Holding the phone for a short call
c: Using voice control or one tap to start or end a call
d: Typing a destination into a handheld GPS
exp: Drivers other than Level 1 and Level 2 may use hands-free or voice-operated features, after one tap or swipe.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Cell phone use

q: Under Michigan's hands-free law, when do points start being added to your record?
d: Never; it is a fine only
exp: A second violation adds 1 point and a third or later adds 2.
src: MCL 257.320a (legislature.mi.gov)

q: Under Michigan's hands-free law, what can a court order after three violations within three years?
exp: Three or more violations within three years can lead to a required driver improvement course.
src: MCL 257.602b (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What happens to a Michigan hands-free fine if the driver caused a crash?
exp: Fines are doubled when the driver using a phone caused a crash.
src: MCL 257.602b (legislature.mi.gov)

q: In Michigan, passengers under what age must wear a seat belt in every seat?
exp: Drivers and front seat passengers must buckle up, and all passengers under 16 must be belted in any seat.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Buckle up

q: Under Michigan's child seat law, children must ride in a car seat or booster until they reach which point?
d: Age 8 or 4 feet 9 inches tall, whichever comes first
exp: Children use a car seat or booster until age 8 or 4 feet 9 inches.
src: MCL 257.710d (legislature.mi.gov); What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Protecting children

q: How many points does reckless driving add to a Michigan driving record?
exp: Reckless driving, OWI and leaving a crash scene each add 6 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: Since the newest Michigan car seat rules, until what age must a child ride rear-facing unless the seat is outgrown?
exp: Children ride rear-facing until age 2 or until they outgrow the seat's limits.
src: MCL 257.710d (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How is Michigan's seat belt law enforced for front seat occupants?
a: Primary: an officer can stop you just for not wearing a belt
b: Secondary: only after a stop for something else
exp: Michigan officers may stop a vehicle when the driver or occupants are not buckled.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 4, Buckle up

q: When may a rear-facing child seat ride in the front seat in Michigan?
a: Whenever the back seat is full
b: If the child is over 1 year old
d: Only if the front passenger airbag is turned off
exp: A rear-facing seat may go in front only with the passenger airbag deactivated.
src: MCL 257.710d (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How many points does a Michigan seat belt ticket add to your record?
exp: Seat belt and child seat violations add no points.
src: MCL 257.710e (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What is the minimum tread depth for passenger car tires in Michigan?
exp: Passenger car tires are unsafe at or below 2/32 inch in two adjacent grooves at three spots.
src: MCL 257.710(h) (legislature.mi.gov)

q: How far down from the top of the windshield may tint or film extend in Michigan?
exp: Tinted film may cover only the top 4 inches of the windshield and of the front side windows.
src: MCL 257.709 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: What are Michigan's default bodily injury liability limits on auto insurance?
exp: The default is 250,000 and 500,000; drivers may choose lower limits of at least 50,000 and 100,000.
src: MCL 500.3009 (legislature.mi.gov)

q: In Michigan, how long do points stay on your driving record?
c: Two years from the conviction date
exp: Points remain for two years from the date of conviction.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: Reaching how many points within two years leads to a Michigan driver reexamination?
exp: Twelve or more points in two years triggers a driver assessment reexamination.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system; Driver reexaminations

q: How many points does careless driving add to a Michigan record?
exp: Careless driving, running a signal or stop sign, and improper passing each add 3 points.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Point system

q: Three crashes within what period can lead to a Michigan driver reexamination?
exp: Three or more crashes over the past two years is one reason for a reexamination.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 2, Driver reexaminations

q: In the Michigan forward stop exercise, how close to the stop line must your front bumper end up?
b: Within 2 feet, without touching or crossing it
exp: Stop with the front bumper within 2 feet of the line, never on or past it.
src: SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)

q: Which of these ends a Michigan driving skills test at once?
a: Speeding 10 mph or more over the limit
b: Asking the examiner to repeat a direction
c: Using both mirrors before a lane change
exp: Speeding 10 mph or more over, running a red light, passing a stopped school bus or any crash is an automatic fail.
src: SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)

q: Who gives the driving skills test in Michigan?
a: A Secretary of State examiner at a branch office
d: An independent driver testing business approved by the Secretary of State
exp: Driving skills tests are given by approved testing businesses, which set their own fees.
src: What Every Driver Must Know (Michigan SOS, Oct. 2025), Ch. 1, Driving skills test

q: Which features may NOT be used during the Michigan driving skills test?
c: Self-parking and other driver-activated assist features
exp: Study aids, phones and driver-activated features such as self-parking are not allowed.
src: SOS, New drivers 18 and older (michigan.gov/sos/license-id/new-drivers-18-older)

q: What does the examiner check during the Michigan vehicle inspection before the road test?
b: Lights, brakes, horn, mirrors, belts, tires and wipers
exp: The vehicle must be safe; failing the inspection ends the test.
src: SOS-360 Driving Skills Test Study Guide (rev. 03/2021)
